question.leadin: Name these New World Colonies now known by their state names.
question.text: Captain John Smith helped to found Jamestown, a settlement within this colony.
question.clue: A deputy governor of this colony issued 81 draconian provisions called Dale's Laws.

swap.leadin: This woman took the name Rebecca after converting to Christianity and later married John Rolfe.
swap.text: In a heavily embellished account, John Smith credited what daughter of Chief Powhatan with saving him from an execution?
swap.clue: Thomas Dale held this figure captive in Henricus following her abduction by Samuel Argall.

question.leadin: This citizen of the Massachusetts Bay Colony was tried in 1637 for "traducing," or slandering, the local ministers.
question.text: Name this 17th-century woman who was sentenced in a trial overseen by John Winthrop for holding prayer sessions for women and speaking out against religious gender norms.
question.clue: After being put on trial during the Antinomian controversy, this person moved to the newly founded Portsmouth colony.

swap.text: This author of The Bloody Tenent of Persecution founded Rhode Island to be a place of religious freedom.
swap.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

question.text: Ivar the Boneless conquered this city, which then became the center of the Danelaw. This city was the birthplace of the scholar Alcuin, who was the head of the palace school at Aachen.
question.clue: Houses named for Lancashire (LAN-kush-er) and this city were the primary factions in the War of the Roses.

swap.leadin: This leader's journal was published as a book titled the "History of New England."
swap.text: Name this Puritan leader, a governor of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, who oversaw the trial of Anne Hutchinson during the Antinomian Controversy.
swap.clue: He sided with Thomas Dudley and John Endecott in a dispute that led to the banishment of John Wheelwright.

question.leadin: An engraving of the Mystic Massacre during this conflict depicts Captain Mason making a breach in the palisade of a town, which is surrounded by archers.
question.text: During what 1630s conflict did English settlers nearly exterminate a namesake tribe led by Sassacus?
question.clue: The Mohawks effectively ended this war after they killed the Grand Sachem Sassacus as a sign of goodwill to the English colonists.

swap.leadin: Established by Charles II, this government's lieutenant governor Francis Nicholson was overthrown in Leisler's Rebellion.
swap.text: Name this government, led by Edmund Andros, that attempted to unite many of the American colonies, and which was overthrown after the Glorious Revolution.
swap.clue: Its first president later became chief justice of New York, and sentenced Jacob Leisler to death for treason.

question.leadin: It began following the deaths of Massasoit and Wamsutta, but more directly due to its namesake anger over John Sassamon's professed love for Jesus.
question.text: Identify this war in which the Wampanoag and Narragansett attacked New England settlements, leading to incidents like the Great Swamp Fight, whose namesake was also known as Metacom.
question.clue: A turning point in this conflict occurred with the Great Swamp Fight, after which the Narragansett were forced to withdraw.

swap.text: It was built after a surprise attack on a group of French soldiers led by commander Jumonville. English forces retreated to Great Meadows and went against Indian counsel to build this fort under the command of George Washington. For 15 points-name this Virginia fort which was taken by the French in 1754, damping English contention in the Ohio valley.
swap.clue: This battle, as well as an earlier incident in a nearby Glen, would prompt the dispatch of the Braddock expedition the following year into the Ohio River Valley.

question.text: This largest slave rebellion in colonial America was led by Jemmy, also known as Cato. This rebellion was put down by the South Carolina militia at the Battle of Edisto River.
question.clue: During this event, participants marched toward Spanish Florida from South Carolina carrying a banner that read "Liberty!"

swap.leadin: During this conflict, the Paxton Boys murdered twenty Susquehannocks at the Conestoga Massacre before being dispersed by Benjamin Franklin.
swap.text: Name this 1763 war which included the Battle of Bloody Run. This war was named for an Ottawa leader who led the Siege of Fort Detroit.
swap.answerHtml: Pontiac’s War [or Pontiac’s Rebellion, accept reasonable equivalents mentioning Pontiac]
swap.clue: Anger at inadequate British defenses during this event led to the massacre of Conestogas by the Paxton Boys.

question.text: The Fundamental Agreement of the New Haven Colony created a court of 16 people with this title, who were "chosen out of the church members." Elected representatives in colonial Virginia also had this title.

swap.leadin: A boy who befriended Richard Pace warned colonists of a 1622 attack by this ruler's brother, Opechancanough [oh-peh-CHAN-ka-"no"], that massacred hundreds.
swap.text: Name this chief of a namesake Algonquian tribal confederation in modern-day Virginia that ruled the region of Tsenacomoco.
swap.clue: He was the high chief among the weorance and held the title of mamanatowick or "emperor" from his capital of Werowocomoco.

question.leadin: This tribe was conned out of its land by the Penn family in the Walking Purchase.
question.text: Name this tribe that agreed to a 1682 treaty with William Penn. Peter Minuit (MIN-yoo-it) convinced members of this tribe to sell him Manhattan Island for some cheap glass beads.
question.clue: This people who lived in the region of the Delaware and Hudson Rivers before European contact. They were defrauded of 1.2 million acres through the Walking Purchase.

swap.leadin: Robert Fogel posited one of these periods spanning roughly the 1960s through 80s, though William G. McLoughlin's thesis about the third period of this type is much more widely accepted.
swap.text: Name these periods of spiritual revival in America, whose first iteration was exemplified by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
swap.answerHtml: Great Awakenings [accept First, Second, Third, or Fourth Great Awakening]
swap.clue: In 1801, over 20,000 people participated in one of these events by attending the Cane Ridge Revival in Kentucky.

question.leadin: He was described as the "torchbearer of the revolution" in a book by Thomas Jefferson Wertenbacker, but that positive interpretation of his major action was opposed in a 1957 book by Wilcomb Washburn.
question.text: Name this revolutionary leader, who defended his actions in a "Declaration of the People" issued at Middle Plantation.
question.clue: This man called an Assembly to stamp out corruption and raise tobacco prices.

swap.leadin: Name some mythical places sought by Spanish explorers.
swap.text: A Zuni referred to as "the Turk" told Coronado of this city in modern day Kansas. Upon reaching this place, Coronado found squash rather than gold.

question.leadin: Among the locations where the provisions of this bill stipulated were acceptable include the taverns of sellers of metheglen, sellers of wine and victualing houses.
question.text: Name this British act that required colonists to perform the namesake action for soldiers; its unfairness inspired the third amendment of the bill of rights.

swap.text: Wampum and beaver pelts were the currency of this colony. This colony was the site of Keift's War and was led by Pieter Stuyvesant for a long time.
swap.clue: This colony which fought with the Algonquin in the Peach Tree War while being led by a man with a pegleg.
